findings.title: Device limit is bypassed after the first rejection because the cache is populated before the DB write
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`) *before* calling `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. With the new limit enforcement, the first request from a device that exceeds the limit returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (and `Anonymous.Authenticate` rejects it), but the key is already cached. Every subsequent request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` within the cache TTL (29 min) short-circuits at the cache check, returns nil, and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded. So the limit only blocks a single request per device per ~29 minutes and is trivially bypassed by a page reload. The cache entry should only be set after a successful store write (or removed on error).

findings.title: Raw `ErrDeviceLimitReached` returned from Authenticate yields an opaque 500 to the user
findings.body: `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is created with `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` in anonstore/database.go and is returned verbatim from `Anonymous.Authenticate`. The authn stack maps non-`errutil` client errors to a generic internal server error, so a user hitting the configured anonymous device limit gets a 500 with no actionable message instead of a well-defined 4xx/403 with a user-facing reason. Define the error with `errutil` (public message, proper status) so the rejection is reported correctly to the browser and logs.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so the device limit can be exceeded
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` first runs `CountDevices` and then, if under the limit, performs the upsert in a separate session. Concurrent requests from different new devices (very likely for anonymous traffic across multiple Grafana instances or goroutines) can all read a count below the limit and all insert, pushing the stored device count above `AnonymousDeviceLimit`. Enforcement needs to be atomic (e.g. insert guarded by a conditional statement/transaction with appropriate locking) if the limit is meant to be a hard cap.

findings.title: Exported provider signatures changed without updating DI wiring / generated code
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` no longer takes `anonstore.AnonStore` but a `db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` gained a second `deviceLimit int64` parameter. These are the providers referenced by the checked-in wire graph (`pkg/server/wire.go` and the generated `wire_gen.go`), plus enterprise wiring. Neither file is part of this PR, so the generated code still calls the old signatures and the build will fail (and/or wire now has a stale `ProvideAnonDBStore` provider with no `int64` binding). Regenerate wire and update all callers. Note this also removes the ability to inject a fake `AnonStore` into the service, which reduces testability of `AnonDeviceService`.

findings.title: Any zero-row UPDATE is reported as "device limit reached"
findings.body: `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `RowsAffected() == 0`. That is true not only for unknown devices but also for a device row that exists yet whose `updated_at` falls outside the `[now-30d, now+1m]` window (rows are only purged after 61 days), and on MySQL for an update that changes no column values. The caller turns this into an authentication failure, so legitimate but stale devices are denied with a misleading error that makes the real cause impossible to diagnose from logs. Distinguish "row not matched" from "limit reached", or at minimum log the device id/reason.

findings.title: New `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` option is undocumented
findings.body: `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `auth.anonymous.device_limit`, but the PR does not add the key to `conf/defaults.ini` / `conf/sample.ini` nor to docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana. Operators have no way to discover the option, its default (0 = unlimited), or the fact that exceeding it blocks anonymous authentication. Grafana convention requires every new ini setting to appear in defaults.ini and the configuration docs. Also consider rejecting/normalizing negative values, which are currently silently treated as "unlimited" by the `s.deviceLimit > 0` check.

findings.title: Limit-enforcement tests do not cover the update path or the client behaviour
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a *new* device is rejected when the limit is reached. The core new logic — that an *existing* device is still updated successfully (and therefore still authenticates) once the limit is hit, including the `updated_at BETWEEN` window boundaries — is untested, as is the new synchronous `Anonymous.Authenticate` behaviour (returns error for `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, logs and continues for other errors) and the interaction with the local cache. Without those tests the limit-bypass via the local cache and the stale-row rejection path go unnoticed.

findings.title: Device tagging moved into the synchronous auth path, adding a COUNT query per cache miss
findings.body: The previous implementation tagged devices in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery; tagging is now done inline on the request's context during `Authenticate`. For every cache miss (once per device per 29 min) an anonymous request now blocks on `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` plus the upsert. `anon_device` has no index supporting a range scan on `updated_at`, so on instances with many anonymous devices this is a table scan in the request path, and any DB slowness/latency is now visible to the user instead of being absorbed asynchronously. Consider caching the count or indexing `updated_at`, and only performing the count when the limit is configured.

findings.title: Backend sends 0 for "no limit" while the frontend type declares `number | undefined`
findings.body: `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` has no `omitempty`/pointer, so when no limit is configured the payload contains `anonymousDeviceLimit: 0`, yet `GrafanaConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit` is typed `number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` initialises it to `undefined`. Frontend code that distinguishes "unset" via `=== undefined` will treat an unlimited instance as having a limit of 0. Use `*int64` with `omitempty` (or document that 0 means unlimited) so the two sides agree.
